quote:
GTA 6 Review: Beautiful but Boring – Relationship Drama Overshadows the Action

Bottom line: technically impressive, but this is no longer "Grand Theft Auto" – it's a long relationship drama with occasional missions thrown in. GTA 5 was far more fun.

After 13 years of waiting, I expected at least the same pace and freedom that GTA 5 gave us. What I got was something else entirely – a game where you spend most of your time watching dialogue, listening to Jason and Lucia talk about their feelings, and only occasionally blowing something up.

What Disappointed Me Most

1. Too many relationships, too little action. This is the core problem. Rockstar clearly wanted a "mature" narrative, but the result is a game where relationship scenes and dialogue take up more time than the missions. GTA 5 had Michael, Franklin, and Trevor – their friction was funny and dynamic, but it never got in the way of the action. Here, the couple's drama just drags the pacing down.

2. Action missions are rare and bland. When you finally get a shooting or heist mission, it feels inserted between long narrative sections rather than being the core of the game. GTA 5's heists were memorable, with planning and choices. GTA 6's missions often feel like "go from point A to point B and watch a cutscene."

3. Slow pacing. The opening hours barely move. The first few hours are almost entirely walking, talking, and everyday routine. I understand it's a deliberate choice, but I wanted to play GTA, not watch a season of a TV series.

4. 30 fps and technical issues. This makes it even worse – the game isn't just slow in pacing, it's also locked at 30 frames per second on consoles, with noticeable drops in dense areas
